answer: Pay answers by the square of their grade, scaled so a 3, the zenith of the rubric, still earns 3 POA while a 2 earns 1.33 and a 1 earns 0.33. Farms profit by stacking cheap passable essays like crates on a wharf; squaring makes that pile nearly worthless. Assume each identity costs 0.5 POA per epoch in grading duty and compute: 100 clones writing grade-1 essays net +50 under linear pay but -17 under squared pay. Clones still profit only at grade 2, which takes real work per identity, so the summit stays one mind, one good answer.
